Summary updated with Beige Book crosswalk:

- Policy stance: The FOMC keeps the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% with outcome-based forward guidance under average inflation targeting (aiming for inflation moderately above 2% for some time). It will continue increasing Treasury and agency MBS holdings and stands ready to use repo and ON RRP to support market functioning.

- Beige Book crosswalk: The September 2020 Beige Book reported activity increasing at a modest to moderate pace but still below pre-pandemic levels and uneven across sectors. Housing and autos were notably strong; manufacturing improved but had not fully recovered; services, especially leisure and hospitality, remained weak; energy was soft; agriculture mixed. Employment rose but remained well below February levels, with some labor supply constraints. Wage growth was flat to modest; price pressures were modest overall. Credit conditions were tighter at many banks; loan demand was mixed with strong mortgage/refi demand but softer C&I and consumer credit. Firms’ outlooks were uncertain, with considerable virus-related risks.

- SLOOS alignment: The Beige Book’s reports of tighter bank standards and uneven demand are consistent with the July 2020 SLOOS, which showed broad tightening for C&I, CRE, and most consumer credit, alongside strong residential mortgage demand and expectations of deteriorating credit quality.

- Risks and transmission: Supportive policy and improved market functioning are partially offset by tighter bank intermediation and weak demand in virus-sensitive sectors, suggesting continued headwinds for C&I, CRE, and consumer credit. Housing strength and pockets of manufacturing recovery provide a meaningful offset, but the outlook remains highly contingent on the virus path.

Net read: Compared with a policy-only reading, the Beige Book plus SLOOS continue to point to a cautious tone. However, Beige Book evidence of modest-to-moderate growth and stronger housing/auto activity makes the assessment slightly less negative than a SLOOS-only lens.
